title: I Challenge a Dev to their OWN Chess Variant (Anarchy Chess)
summary: Tony plays two online games of 'Anarchy Chess' (based on r/AnarchyChess memes) against its developer 'slomg' (~1200 rating), with commentary from both POVs. The 10x10 blue/cream board uses cartoon hand-drawn pieces and many meme rules: underage pawns, knooks from 'nuclear fusion', long passant, bouncing bishops, shared/title rooks, an inverse queen, a checkers piece, and 'bored' pieces that leave the board when you are out of time. Tony wins game 1 (~12:46) and loses game 2 in time-trouble chaos (~21:10).
rules: 10x10 board (counted from frames), cartoon meme pieces.
Pawns may move up to three squares at a time; a pawn can be dragged back onto a piece and 'launched' forward (as described ~1:53).
Underage pawn: if it is in the line of sight of ANY bishop (own or enemy), that bishop must capture it.
Nuclear fusion: a knight and rook landing on the same square fuse into a Knook (knight + rook, but rook movement limited to 2 squares). Double-clicking can 'super fuse' pieces.
Long passant: en passant captures can be chained for multiple captures.
Bishops bounce off the board edges (reflecting diagonals); a bounced attack can prevent castling.
Shared 'title' rooks: neutral rooks controlled by whichever side has a piece adjacent to them.
Inverse queen: moves everywhere a queen does not (effectively knight-like).
Checkers piece: a piece that moves/captures like a checker.
Clock: 30 s for the first move; when your time runs out you enter 'overtime' where your pieces get bored and start leaving the board one by one instead of flagging.
win_condition: Checkmate/capture the opponent's king (normal chess goal within Anarchy rules).
